text:
matt: heads-up — after the continuous-batching change landed last night i’m seeing prefix cache hit-rate drop for short prompts. p95 latency for small-chat route jumped ~40ms. not huge but reproducible across nodes

sarah: ugh. repro on staging? can you paste the cache stats and a minimal repro?

matt: repro on staging + a subset of prod traces. quick snapshot from staging run:
```
route: small-chat
batcher: continuous-v3
cache_prefix_hits: 76.8%
cache_prefix_misses: 23.2%
avg_warmup_tokens_on_miss: 135
p50_latency: 46ms -> 52ms
p95_latency: 180ms -> 220ms
```

leo: interesting — continuous batching increases composition variance. more heterogeneous batches means prefixes are less likely to align, so higher miss rate. did we change keying or TTL?

matt: no TTL change. keying same SHA(prefix+model+ver). suspect queueing/batch composition causing earlier requests to be flushed before their prefix is available in cache (warmup not finished).

ana: (typo: ana) can you share profiler trace? curious if kernel selection/first-token overhead got worse for warmup path.

matt: profiler snippet (trimmed):
```
[warmup] token_gen_kernel_select: 12us
[kv_populate] kv_write_latency: 8.3ms
[kv_lock_wait] avg: 2.1ms
[serve] actual_decode_kernel: 6us
```

leo: kv_write_latency of 8.3ms stands out. continuous batching might be doing more concurrent KV writes which triggers locks/serialization. that would delay cache visibility for following reqs in the same batch window.

sarah: do we have any recent kernel-selection changes that could impact warmup cost? e.g., fallback to slower kernels for short sequences?

ana: kernel selection hasn't changed for small-chat. but we did alter the scheduler to favor throughput (slightly larger batches) which could increase the # of concurrent warmups. also continuous-batcher tries to pack based on arrival time, not prefix affinity.

leo: possible mitigations: 1) bias batching to co-locate same-prefix or same-model versions for X ms, 2) soft cap concurrent KV writes (throttle warmup writers), 3) best-effort pre-warm for top-N prefixes observed per minute.

matt: ran quick experiment toggling affinity-shuffle off (i.e., prefer prefix affinity). hit-rate jumped to 89% and p95 dropped ~30ms. downside: some requests wait longer while we try to pack affinity groups.

sarah: that matches intuition. tradeoff: latency vs hit-rate (and cost). we need numbers across QPS levels. can you run perf matrix? small/med/large qps with affinity on/off and max-batch-size config?

ci-bot: perf job queued: job/continuous-prefix-warmup/1862501234 (link: https://ci.internal/jobs/1862501234)

ana: add another axis: compare kernel warmup penalty when warmup is done under quantized kernels vs fp16 kernels. quantized kernels can have different init overheads.

leo: also check KV keying microbench — maybe our key object has grown (we recently added route metadata) which increased hashing time and caused lock contention. micro-optimizing key serialization could shave a ms or two.

matt: good call. microbench of key hashing:
```
old: 0.8us per key
new-with-route-meta: 2.9us per key
```
that explains some of the extra cost but not the multi-ms kv_write latency.

sarah: action list:
- matt: run perf matrix (affinity on/off, batch windows 5/10/20ms, qps tiers) — link above queued
- leo: add instrumentation around KV write concurrency + locks, dump histograms
- ana: test kernel warmup cost across fp16/quant/uint8 kernels for warmup paths
- infra: consider a short-term change to prefer prefix affinity in continuous-batcher for routes with high prefix-hit value

matt: will do. if we can get affinity heuristics into the next deploy, we can mitigate reg immediately. for long-term: consider asynchronous pre-warm pipeline (best-effort cache put via sidecar).

ana: one more note — we should avoid making affinity absolute: a probabilistic affinity (e.g., prefer same-prefix 70% of the time) might keep throughput while improving hit-rate. also can prioritize based on expected token length (short prompts > more benefit from hits).

leo: agree. let's treat it as multi-objective optimization: minimize cost per token subject to p95 latency SLO. we need experiment matrices to fit a simple model.

sarah: cool. keep updates in this thread and paste perf graphs when done. thanks all. :thumbsup:
